title: Eppendorf Research plus operating manual
locator: Sections 4.1–4.2 and 6.1–6.5 on immersion and operation. Sections 11.4 and 12.2 on test conditions and single-channel order codes.
summary: The manual covers tip selection, setting the transfer volume, immersion depth and forward dispensing. Its single-channel ordering table identifies the 20–200 µL and 100–1,000 µL versions separately.
scope: Choose the range printed on the pipette. The manufacturer's test conditions include a calibrated analytical balance, evaporation protection and ten repeated deliveries per volume.
rights: Original summary of the manufacturer-hosted operating manual.

title: Standard Testing Procedure for Manual Dispensing Systems
locator: Sections 7.4, 7.5.1–7.5.2 and 7.6 on preparation, mechanical single-channel testing and mass-to-volume conversion. Research plus variable-volume error tables, pp. 73–74.
summary: Eppendorf describes weighing repeated water deliveries and converting the measurements to volume. The tables give the testing volumes, tip type and separate limits for systematic and random error for each Research plus size.
scope: Select the row for the pipette, test tip and volume actually used. Balance suitability and evaporation control affect a gravimetric delivery check, especially at the low end of the range.
rights: Original summary of the manufacturer's published test procedure.

title: The Calibration and Use of Piston Pipettes
version: Blues, Bayliss and Buckley, Measurement Good Practice Guide No. 69
locator: Sections 7.2–7.5, pp. 13–17, on apparatus, procedure and calculations. Section 8, including Table 2, on sources of uncertainty.
summary: The guide shows how to weigh replicate deliveries of water, select a balance for the volume, and estimate the delivered volume and repeatability. A worked uncertainty budget covers contributions from the water, weighing and environment.
scope: The guide uses the 2002 ISO 8655 framework. Apply the appropriate current instrument specification when making a conformity decision.
rights: Original summary and link to the national measurement laboratory's published guide.

title: Serial Dilutions and Standard Curves with a Microplate Readers
publisher: Biology LibreTexts, San Diego State University course collection
locator: Part 1, Materials and Procedure, including two-, four- and five-fold series. Part II, Measuring Absorbance, and Part III, Standard Curves.
summary: The exercise uses a P200 micropipette, food dye and a 96-well plate. It lays out the dilution factors and mixing steps and shows how to read absorbance and plot the standard curve.
scope: Use a compatible clear plate and a reader wavelength suited to the dye. Several transfers are below 100 µL. A 100–1,000 µL pipette cannot carry out that series as written.
rights: Shannon Clark's course material is published under CC BY 4.0. Original summary.

title: Serial Dilutions – Tube Method
locator: Page 1, Materials, Procedure steps 1–8 and Interpretation.
summary: The procedure follows a dye through six successive two-fold dilutions with water. Each tube receives a 1 mL transfer, making it a visual check of mixing and serial dilution technique with a P1000.
scope: The source specifies a prepared blue dye. The stated transfer exceeds the range of a 200 µL pipette. The visual progression is qualitative. Measuring dilution precision requires replicate optical measurements with a suitable dye and reader.
rights: Original summary of the university-hosted method.

title: Pipette Olympics: An Engaging Exercise for Undergraduate Laboratory Training
locator: Materials and Methods, protocol steps 1–16 and Figure 1. Tables 1–3 show the dilution curve, replicate precision and three students' repeated attempts.
summary: The authors measured tartrazine food dye in a microplate to assess serial dilution linearity and used replicate wells to assess pipetting precision. The paper includes a plate map, sample absorbances and results from three students who repeated the exercise.
scope: The protocol specifies both 20–200 µL and 100–1,000 µL pipettes and a plate reader capable of measuring the dye's absorbance. Replicate variation and curve fit assess technique. Absolute delivery accuracy needs a separate reference.
rights: Original summary with a link to the journal and its full article.

title: Strategies to Maintain Sample Integrity Using a Liquid-Filled Automated Liquid-Handling System with Fixed Pipetting Tips
publisher: Journal of the Association for Laboratory Automation
locator: Results and discussion, Table 2, manual pipettors compared by gravimetry and dual-dye photometry. The automated comparison appears separately in Table 1.
summary: Table 2 gives 36 manual deliveries at each of four target volumes from 20 to 200 µL. At 100 µL the mean measured by weighing was 100.39 µL and the optical mean was 100.43 µL.
scope: Use the manual comparison in Table 2 for a micropipette. The subsequent serial dilution experiments used an automated fixed-tip instrument. The photometric comparison required an Artel dual-dye measurement system.
rights: Original summary of the research and link to the journal-hosted article.

title: Calibration of Micropipettes through Gravimetric Solution and its Beneficial Impact on Research
locator: Materials and Methods, selected volumes and water-weighing procedure. Results, Table 2 and Figure 2, the 1,000 µL control chart.
summary: The authors checked water deliveries at 200, 500 and 1,000 µL with an analytical balance and compared systematic and random errors to the stated limits. The 1,000 µL series supplies an example control chart.
scope: The paper describes the volume range without identifying an Eppendorf model. Its historical acceptance table describes the study. Use the applicable local limits and instrument documentation for a new check.
rights: Original summary and link to the publisher's full article.

title: Pipetting Performance across Laboratory Personnel: A Comparative Study
publisher: The Journal of Applied Laboratory Medicine
locator: Materials and Methods, pipette ranges and spectrophotometric dilution task. Consult the dilution results separately from the gravimetric experiment in Table 2.
summary: The researchers paired 20–200 µL and 100–1,000 µL Eppendorf Research plus pipettes to prepare colored solutions from a stock and compare dilution performance among 108 operators.
scope: This task measured copper sulfate against a water blank at 635 nm on a Lambda 365. Separate mixtures from the stock assess direct dilution. A serial dilution can accumulate transfer errors across steps. The paper's water-weighing task used a third, 10–100 µL pipette.
rights: Original summary of the authors' study and link to the publisher via its DOI.
